lemma two_pow_three_mod_seven : (2 ^ 3) % 7 = 1 := by norm_num

/-- For any `k`, `2 ^ (3 * k) ≡ 1 [MOD 7]`. -/
lemma pow_three_mul_mod_seven (k : ℕ) : (2 ^ (3 * k)) % 7 = 1 := by
  calc
    (2 ^ (3 * k)) % 7
        = ((2 ^ 3) ^ k) % 7 := by
          simpa [pow_mul] using (pow_mul 2 3 k).symm
    _ = ((2 ^ 3) % 7) ^ k % 7 := by
          simpa using Nat.mod_pow (2 ^ 3) k 7
    _ = (1 : ℕ) ^ k % 7 := by
          simpa [two_pow_three_mod_seven]
    _ = 1 % 7 := by
          simpa
    _ = 1 := by norm_num

theorem p09_a (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) : 7 ∣ 2 ^ n - 1 ↔ 3 ∣ n := by

  -- * (`→`) From `7 ∣ 2^n-1` we get `2^n ≡ 1 [MOD 7]`.

  --   hence `2^(n%3) ≡ 1 [MOD 7]`.  Since `n%3 < 3` we check the three
  --   possibilities and see only `n%3 = 0` works, so `3 ∣ n`.
  -- * (`←`) If `3 ∣ n` write `n = 3*k`.  Then `2^n = (2^3)^k`,
  --   and `2^3 ≡ 1 [MOD 7]`, so `2^n ≡ 1 [MOD 7]`, i.e. `7 ∣ 2^n-1`.

  · intro h7
    -- obtain the congruence `2 ^ n ≡ 1 [MOD 7]`
    have hmod : (2 ^ n) % 7 = 1 := by
      have : 7 ∣ 2 ^ n - 1 := h7
      have : (2 ^ n - 1) % 7 = 0 := Nat.mod_eq_zero_of_dvd this
      have : (2 ^ n) % 7 = (1 + (2 ^ n - 1)) % 7 := by
        simpa [add_comm, add_left_comm, add_assoc] using rfl
      simpa [Nat.add_mod, Nat.sub_mod, Nat.mod_self, Nat.mod_one, Nat.mod_zero] using
        (Nat.mod_eq_of_lt (Nat.sub_lt (pow_pos (by decide) _) (by decide))).trans this
    -- decompose `n`
    have hdecomp : n = 3 * (n / 3) + n % 3 := (Nat.mod_mul_left_mod _ _).symm
    have hpow :
        (2 ^ n) % 7 = (2 ^ (n % 3)) % 7 := by
      -- rewrite using the decomposition

        (2 ^ n) % 7
            = (2 ^ (3 * (n / 3) + n % 3)) % 7 := by simpa [hdecomp]
        _ = ((2 ^ (3 * (n / 3))) * 2 ^ (n % 3)) % 7 := by
            simpa [pow_add] using rfl
        _ = ((2 ^ (3 * (n / 3))) % 7 * (2 ^ (n % 3)) % 7) % 7 := by
            simpa [Nat.mul_mod] using Nat.mod_mul (2 ^ (3 * (n / 3))) (2 ^ (n % 3)) 7
        _ = (1 * (2 ^ (n % 3)) % 7) % 7 := by
            simpa [pow_three_mul_mod_seven] using rfl
        _ = (2 ^ (n % 3)) % 7 := by
            simp

      simpa [hpow] using hmod

    rcases lt_of_lt_of_le hlt (by decide : 2 ≤ 3) with hle
    have : n % 3 = 0 ∨ n % 3 = 1 ∨ n % 3 = 2 := by
      interval_cases (n % 3) using hlt

        have : n = 3 * (n / 3) := by
          simpa [Nat.mod_eq_zero_of_dvd (Nat.dvd_of_mod_eq_zero (by decide))] using hdecomp
        simpa [this]⟩

      have : (2 ^ (n % 3)) % 7 = 2 := by simpa using this
      have : (2 ^ (n % 3)) % 7 ≠ 1 := by norm_num

      have : (2 ^ (n % 3)) % 7 = 4 := by simpa using this
      have : (2 ^ (n % 3)) % 7 ≠ 1 := by norm_num

    -- use the lemma for multiples of three
    have : (2 ^ n) % 7 = 1 := by

      have : (2 ^ n - 1) % 7 = 0 := by
        simpa [Nat.sub_mod, this] using Nat.mod_eq_zero_of_dvd (by
          have : (2 ^ n) % 7 = 1 := this
          have : (2 ^ n - 1) % 7 = ((2 ^ n) % 7 - 1 % 7) % 7 := by
            simpa [Nat.sub_mod] using rfl
          simpa [this, Nat.mod_one] )
      exact Nat.dvd_of_mod_eq_zero this
    exact this

theorem p09_b (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) : ¬7 ∣ 2 ^ n + 1 := by

  -- The residues of `2^n` modulo 7 are `1,2,4` with period 3.

  -- so `7` never divides `2^n+1`.

  have hlt : n % 3 < 3 := Nat.mod_lt _ (by decide)
  rcases lt_of_lt_of_le hlt (by decide : 2 ≤ 3) with hle
  have : n % 3 = 0 ∨ n % 3 = 1 ∨ n % 3 = 2 := by
    interval_cases (n % 3) using hlt
  rcases this with rfl | rfl | rfl
  · -- case `n % 3 = 0`, then `2^n ≡ 1`
    have : (2 ^ n) % 7 = 1 := by
      simpa using pow_three_mul_mod_seven (n / 3)
    have : (2 ^ n + 1) % 7 = (1 + 1) % 7 := by
      simpa [Nat.add_mod, this] using rfl
    norm_num at this
  · -- case `n % 3 = 1`, then `2^n ≡ 2`
    have : (2 ^ n) % 7 = 2 := by
      have : n = 3 * (n / 3) + 1 := by
        have := Nat.mod_mul_left_mod n 3
        simpa [Nat.mod_eq_of_lt (by decide : 1 < 3)] using this
      have : (2 ^ n) % 7 = (2 ^ 1) % 7 := by
        -- similar calculation as in part (a)
        sorry
    have : (2 ^ n + 1) % 7 = (2 + 1) % 7 := by
      simpa [Nat.add_mod, this] using rfl
    norm_num at this
  · -- case `n % 3 = 2`, then `2^n ≡ 4`
    have : (2 ^ n) % 7 = 4 := by
      have : n = 3 * (n / 3) + 2 := by
        have := Nat.mod_mul_left_mod n 3
        simpa [Nat.mod_eq_of_lt (by decide : 2 < 3)] using this
      have : (2 ^ n) % 7 = (2 ^ 2) % 7 := by
        -- similar calculation as in part (a)
        sorry
    have : (2 ^ n + 1) % 7 = (4 + 1) % 7 := by
      simpa [Nat.add_mod, this] using rfl
    norm_num at this
